I [22m] have not idea what to do about my fiancee [21f] and our life thus far (update)

You two have been together from a young age and have not only shared your entire high school experience, you've shared numerous life experiences. You're engaged. Your families are practically one. It is going to be extremely difficult for her, and for you at times too.

The best thing you can do - for both of you - is to be honest. With her and with yourself. There are going to be a lot of tears, and probably quite a few angry words. Answer questions. Get her tissues. Explain to her in the best way that you know how.

Know that you won't have her back as a friend for quite some time, if ever. You're both going to need space once this is done to digest everything. You're going to need time to process the end of this too and that's totally ok. She's definitely going to need time. So much time. Take time to grieve and keep your distance! I said grieve for a reason: losing a relationship like this is akin to mourning the death of a loved one. In fact, that's exactly what's happening; you're both losing the relationship that you've shared for 7 years. The relationship, the life you've built together, has died.

As much as you want to keep her as a friend, right now you can't be that for her. I can't stress it enough: give her space, don't make yourself available, and know that you aren't who she needs for comfort right now. That last bit is the hardest, as you obviously care for her and don't want to see her hurt. She doesn't want to hurt either, and is going to be confused as you're the person she's shared so much with over the past 7 years. You aren't that person anymore. You can't be. It's best for both of you if you aren't.

[That's just my two cents after being dumped from a 5+ year relationship in which we'd discussed marriage and made plans for our future. I felt like my entire life was crashing down and have been trying to re-build a life alone since then.]

Too add to these ideas, which are great, allow yourself time to process what you're going through. Try not to be rash with your words or action, give pause, and breath. If you are not ready to talk about what's going on, that's okay, but eventually you will need to build a narrative of what happened. Talk to your friends and family... And internet friends :)
It is for the best to resolve this now than years down the line, possibly with children, in a situation where there is never any happiness. Hopefully things continue to work out in a positive way.
This must be a trying time for you, but as others have mentioned it's best to figure this out while you're still young. Best of luck in the days/months ahead. :)

I think you should both break up and allow each of you to explore other parts of relationships and new experiences.

Love is not a race that you must hold on to no matter what for life.

Love is a series of events with different people you enjoy and maybe in the end someone will stick long enough.

Got bored before work this past week and came up with my own Western Conference power rankings. I watched more Western Conference games than anything last year, and I’m more of a West Coast guy anyways. Rankings are based on my own personal projections and thoughts for the upcoming season and meant to be fun. Enjoy!

Western Conference Power Rankings:

GS Warriors My biggest concerns for this team heading into next season are: (1) can they keep up their preferred pace of play after the long season and (2) how will they adapt to going from the hunter to the hunted. They still have the most depth in the league along with what seems like the most cohesive roster and barring any unforeseen injuries or circumstances, the Warriors will be in contention for another title this season.

OKC Thunder They don’t deserve this, but hey, everyone is entitled to a stupid bet every now and then if all they have to wager is their pride. I am a believer in Billy Donovan being the right asshole to turn Kevin Durant into the forward version of Steph Curry and keep Russell Westbrook focused and engaged long enough to not settle for pullup jumpers with 19 on the clock. They are the league’s best bets to be this year’s Warriors.

SA Spurs I’m lukewarm on the LMA and David West signings. Good players who fit the Spurs M.O., but I’m just not sure if they push the needle. Ultimately, I think this team’s success is dependent on how Kawhi Leonard continues to evolve as a player.

LA Clippers Here’s what the Clippers needed the most these last two seasons: a capable one on one scorer, a competent bench, and some grit to help toughen up a team of whiny bitches. They addressed all of these needs in the off-season by signing Paul Pierce, re-signing DeAndre Jordan, and (in my Most Underrated Move of the Summer) trading for Lance Stephenson. With the emergence of Austin Rivers as a capable offensive player off the bench, the next logical move for LAC is to trade Jamal Crawford for a backup defensive minded big. I don’t know if this is a championship team, but it’s definitely the best roster Chris Paul has ever had to work with.

New Orleans Pelicans They’ve put together a great roster over the past few seasons. There doesn’t seem to be any holes in terms of on court personnel: they have a great blend of talent and depth at every position. I like the hiring of Alvin Gentry. He should be able to take that talent and create a system and team that is better than mediocre offensively.

Houston Rockets I think this roster peaked last season. Harden has handled the offensive load on his own for three straight years now. Houston has a great collection of role players, but if they want to take it to the next level, someone needs to step up and be more than a catch and shoot threat or they need to acquire a better second player. Dwight Howard seems content with being a defensive specialist.

Memphis Grizzlies I watched more Memphis basketball than any other team not named the Clippers last season and it turned me into an unabashedly biased Marc Gasol fan. He cracked top five in my personal MVP and DPOY voting. Memphis has a decent roster, but it’s a lot of players who have specific skills, kind of like the conservative defensive-oriented version of Houston. There’s no real all-around talent on that team, no guy who can get the ball one on one on the perimeter and make a move or two and score. Jeff Green is overrated, Courtney Lee is Diet JJ Redick, Vince Carter is a geriatric, and Tony Allen handles the ball like it is has lumps on the surface. Should the core of Gasol, Conley, and Randolph stay healthy, I’m optimistic they win 50+ games and make the playoffs. But Gasol and Randolph are both on the wrong side of 30 and Conley is kind of fragile. They are one tough break away from being a lottery team.

Denver Nuggets I followed Mike Malone’s tenure in Sacramento from the beginning, and I think he’s great at creating a positive playing environment. I didn’t follow Denver as closely as other teams these last two years, but from the outside, they look like a mess. Still, the roster is talented and most of the key players on this team have been to the playoffs. I think Malone is the perfect coach to come in right away and excavate that chip on the team’s collective shoulder.

Sacramento Kings The Kings are catching flack for running their operation like a dysfunctional rec league team, but I will give credit where it is due: for the first time in years, it looks like they have a talented team. All across the roster are the names of players who have proven they can play in the NBA. Rajon Rondo may have stopped caring last season, but I don’t think he’s done by any means. He’ll be running the show in Sacramento. Darren Collison proved he was more than capable of starting last season, but Rondo’s craftiness will better serve guys like Cousins and Gay. The realistic best case scenario for this team is everyone rallies together with something to prove and they make the playoffs, maybe even win a series (or at least make it interesting.) The worst case scenario is somewhere between a fire sale by Christmas and players getting locked up for choking each other.

Utah Jazz Statistically, they were the best defensive team in the league. Every time I watched them play last year, it just looked like they tried harder than their opponents. But they’re still young and they don’t have an established point guard. I would be surprised to see Utah take the next step and make the playoffs this season.

LA Lakers I think the Lakers went out and got Roy Hibbert because they want to commit to a lineup of Clarkson, Russell, Kobe, and Randle, and Hibbert makes up for the lack of size at every other position. Maybe Brandon Bass starts instead of Julius Randle, but either way, having Lou Williams and Jordan Hill along with either Randle or Bass off the bench is actually a big improvement over the crap the Lakers have trotted out there last season.

Minnesota Timberwolves There is just so much talent on this team that it wouldn’t be surprising to see them commit to playing the veterans and try to make the playoffs OR see them unload some of the older guys and play the youngsters while preparing for the future. I have their wins in the 30’s. My prediction is they wait til next off-season to unload the veterans Pekovic, Rubio, and Martin, and then hand the team over to Coach Tom Thibodeau.

Dallas Mavericks You can’t really blame the Mavericks for being on cruise control since they won their title in 2011. These last four off-seasons have been filled with the promise of signing a big name free agent, only to strike out or overpay against themselves for role players. I suspect a down year for Dallas on the court this season.

Phoenix Suns It feels like a transitional year for the Suns, who have done some major retooling of the roster in the past year.

Portland Blazers I’m calling it now: Damian Lillard leads the league in field goal attempts per game this season with over 23.

Hey all o/ I'm new to Voat, but I used to hang out on r/gamedev back in the day and thought I'd make my first post in this sub.

Glide is a tweening engine inspired by Actuate and Tweenlite. I started it a few years ago when I moved from Flash to C# and realized that the available options were sadly limited. I've been working on it ever since. It's now part of Kyle Pulver's Otter2d framework, and it's being used in Blossom Tales: The Sleeping King and casino games by Eclipse Gaming Systems (I'm not privy to the details on this one, unfortunately).

Here's a quick rundown of the kind of things it can do:

The Basics

// create a tweener
var Tweener = new Tweener();

// use it to tween stuff...
// This tween will move the X and Y properties of the target
Tweener.Tween(target, new { X = toX, Y = toY }, duration, delay);

// ...or set up timed callbacks
Tweener.Timer(duration, delay).OnComplete(CompleteCallback);

// every frame, update the tweener
// I use fractional seconds in a float, but you can use anything you want as long as you're consistent
Tweener.Update(frameTime);

Behavior

You can specify a number of special behaviors for a tween to use. Calls can be chained for setting more than one at a time.

// Glide comes with a full complement of easing functions
Tweener.Tween(...).Ease(Ease.ElasticOut);

Tweener.Tween(...).OnComplete(() => Console.WriteLine("done"));
Tweener.Tween(...).OnUpdate(() => Console.WriteLine("updating"));

// Repeat twice
Tweener.Tween(...).Repeat(2);

// Repeat forever
Tweener.Tween(...).Repeat();

// Reverse the tween every other time it repeats
Tweener.Tween(...).Repeat().Reflect();

// Swaps the end and start values of a tween.
// This is helpful if you want to set an object's properties to one set of values, and then tween back to the previous values.
Tweener.Tween(...).Reverse();

// Smoothly interpolate a rotation value past the end of an axis.
Tweener.Tween(...).Rotation();

// Round tweened properties to integer values
Tweener.Tween(...).Round();

Control

If you need to control tweens after they are launched (for example, pausing or cancelling), you can hold a reference to the object returned By Tween():

var myTween = Tweener.Tween(object, new {X = toX, Y = toY}, duration);

You can later use this object to control the tween:

myTween.Cancel();
myTween.CancelAndComplete();

myTween.Pause();
myTween.PauseToggle();

myTween.Resume();

Calling a control method on a tweener will affect all tweens it manages.

If you'd rather not keep tween controller objects around, you can also control them by passing an object being tweened to a target control function.

Tweener.Tween(myObject, ...);

Tweener.TargetCancel(myObject);
Tweener.TargetCancelAndComplete(myObject);

Tweener.TargetPause(myObject);
Tweener.TargetPauseToggle(myObject);

Tweener.TargetResume(myObject);

Custom lerpers

By default, Glide only knows how to tween numeric values, but with a little help it can work with any type in your project. For value types whose properties can't be modified with reflection, you can create a custom lerper class to inform Glide of how to handle tweens that involve types like XNA's Vector3 or SFML's Color struct.

After your lerpers are configured, using non-numeric types looks exactly like any other tween:

Tweener.Tween(target, new { Position = new Vector2(toX, toY) }, duration, delay);

That's about all there is to it! I hope you find it useful. Please let me know if you have any questions, feature requests, etc. :)
